messages:
Jordan: kicking off a short canary to validate the takeover path when we demote+rehandoff hot prefixes. want to flush out any accounting or correctness holes early
Priya: nice. which scenarios? sudden owner crash, overlapping preclaims, and churn?
Jordan: all three. plus slow network where apply succeeds but acknowledgement is delayed.
Sam: key concern: eviction-credit charging. if we debit credits on preclaim and then fail to apply, customers get billed without capacity. we've seen billing disputes before.
Len: imo debit should happen only on a confirmed ownership transition. preclaim should reserve a lightweight marker but not consume tenant credits. downside: we could have many pending preclaims that starve the real eviction pool.
Maya: tradeoff idea: two-level tokens: (a) soft-reserve token (cheap, many allowed per-node), (b) committed credit (strict, limited). Only commit on apply_confirm. That avoids overbilling while bounding outstanding preclaims.
Sam: sounds good. need clear invariants though: committed credits must always be <= tenant_quota and we must be able to refund if a committed apply is later rolled back. refunds are painful. better to avoid committing until final.
Priya: refund complexity argues for commit-on-confirm only. For fairness, limit soft-reserve per-node-per-shard to e.g., 8. enforce in rebalancer.
Jordan: agreed. implement soft-reserve with backpressure in rebalancer. will add metric "kv.soft_reserve_count{node,shard}" and throttle when >8.
Len: correctness: we must avoid split-brain where two nodes both see a confirmed apply. pack the state and CAS it atomically: pack = (epoch<<48) | owner_id<<32 | nonce_hash. single CAS on packed_state ensures linearizability.
Maya: example pack helper: ```// pack: [64-bit epoch][32-bit owner][32-bit nonce_hash]
uint128_t pack = (uint128_t(epoch) << 64) | (uint128_t(owner) << 32) | nonce_hash;
if (CAS(&packed_state, expected_pack, new_pack)) { /* success */ }
```
Sam: also enforce monotonic nonces per node so new takeover > old takeover via numeric compare. store last_nonce per node to avoid reuse.
Priya: performance: packed CAS check on write path? we can't CAS every write. solution: read cached_packed_state from memory with RCU and validate periodically. on mismatch, reject writes or forward to sequencer.
Jordan: route writes during takeover to the sequencer which consults the authority. sequencer will check cached epoch first and then, if stale, fetch packed_state. that keeps fast path lean.
Len: add a short-lived read-tag: when ownership is recent (<TTL), reads are allowed from old owner but marked stale. writes go to sequencer. TTL configurable per-tenant.
Maya: telemetry plan: emit counters: ownership_transitions_total{outcome=success|conflict|timeout}, soft_reserve_count, committed_eviction_debits_total, preclaim_latency_bucket. also sample traces with tag takeover_id.
ops-bot: canary started on shard s-21 at 2024-09-03T09:12. watch /metrics/kv/ownership and /traces/service=kv_handshake
Sam: tests: unit: packed-state CAS semantics + nonce monotonicity. integration: chaos test that kills old owner after apply (ensure no double-commit). property: idempotency of apply RPCs.
Priya: add billing integration test: simulate preclaim->abort, ensure no committed debit; simulate apply_confirm after long delay, ensure debit happens exactly once.
Jordan: I'll draft PR for soft-reserve + packed-CAS + sequencer-write-routing. Maya: can you own metrics naming and alert thresholds?
Maya: yes. propose alert when ownership_transitions_total{conflict}>5/min or soft_reserve_count per node > 6 for >60s.
Len: docs: update prefix-cache/ownership.md with new packed format, invariants (no double-commit, commit-on-confirm), and read/write routing rules. include example failure diagrams.
Sam: one more edge: clock skew + stale nonce timestamps. rely solely on monotonic nonce counters, not timestamps, for ordering. timestamps for telemetry only.
Priya: ok owners: Jordan implement code + integration tests; Maya metrics+alerts; Len docs; Sam test harness and property tests. timeline: feature branch by Mon, PR review midweek.
Jordan: ack. will tag the group in PR and add a short demo gif in the PR showing takeover timeline. thanks everyone :rocket:
